title: A leader that takes a late acceptance as news moves a follower back, proved safe
summary: A Raft leader ignores an acceptance of entries it has already recorded the follower as holding: a late or repeated reply moves nothing backwards. A developer has the leader take the follower's word whenever it comes, late or not: an acceptance says what the follower held when it answered, the record follows it, and the next request carries what the follower has already, which it accepts again. The tests pass, the contract diff is one row, and the change is verified under all four configurations, the three in which an RPC is one step and the one in which a reply waits on the wire and may be handed to the leader twice, which is the one in which the changed row does anything: a leader with an empty log whose heartbeat a follower accepts, which then appends an entry and replicates it, and is handed the heartbeat's acceptance again, records the follower as holding nothing and sends the entry again, which the follower accepts a second time. The record says less than the follower holds, never more, and the commit rule, which counts the record, counts fewer servers than hold the entry, never more.

change.description: In `ReplyRule.decide`, the `ANSWERED` arm returns `transition(ANSWERED, ADVANCE)` for an acceptance instead of `unchanged`, with the comment that an acceptance is the follower's own word on what it holds, late or not; a refusal answered already still changes nothing. The javadoc is reworded to match, and the test that a late or repeated reply changes nothing is split: an acceptance is followed whenever it comes, a late refusal changes nothing.

risk: Low, and the question a reviewer asks is the one example 103 answers in the other direction: whether a reply the record has answered already can be taken as news without the record going wrong. For a refusal it cannot; for an acceptance the record goes down, to what the follower held when it answered, which it still holds, since within a term only this leader writes the follower's log and only appends to it. The one-step configurations cannot tell this change from the committed rule, since the only answered acceptance they hand the rule is a heartbeat's, through the index the record holds already, which the patched row moves to where it is. The delayed replies configuration is the one in which a late acceptance reaches below the record.
explanation: The reply rule in the model is generated from the regenerated contract, so an acceptance answered already moves the follower's match index to the last entry it accepted and its next index past it. TLC verifies the change under all four configurations: 20,253, 8,838 and 14,388 states under the three one-step configurations, the same as the committed rule's, since the changed row is taken there only by the heartbeat a caught-up follower accepts, which moves the record to where it is; and 605,428 states under `RaftReplicationDelayed.cfg`, more than the committed rule's 261,060, since the record now goes back on a late acceptance and the leader sends again. Every invariant holds, `MatchIndexIsRight` and `NextIndexPastMatch` among them: the record never says more than the follower holds, and the next index stays past the match index, since the two move together.
resolution: Merge, if the round trips are acceptable. Taking a late acceptance as the follower's current state is wrong in general and safe here: the record understates what the follower holds, which costs the leader a request the follower accepts again and the commit rule a server it could have counted, and overstates nothing. A reviewer who wants the record monotonic has etcd's MaybeUpdate to point to, which takes the maximum; a reviewer who wants the cheapest rule has this one. What the verification settles is that neither choice can commit an entry a majority does not hold.
provenance: Constructed as the third example of the reply rule, to pair with 103: the same row's neighbour changed the same way, safe this time, which the one-step configurations cannot tell from 103 and the delayed replies configuration tells apart.

references.title: Ongaro and Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (extended version, 2014): section 5.3, log replication, the consistency check, and the nextIndex and matchIndex a leader keeps per follower; figure 2, the rules for leaders on an AppendEntries reply

Ongaro, the TLA+ specification of Raft (raft.tla): HandleAppendEntriesResponse, which moves nextIndex and matchIndex on success and decrements nextIndex on failure, and messages as a bag, so that a reply may be delivered after another
etcd raft, tracker/progress.go: MaybeUpdate and MaybeDecrTo, which ignore a stale acceptance (an index at or below Match) and a stale rejection (one that does not answer the request at Next - 1)
